title: mitigate multi-region coldstart throughput drop
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Customer escalations reported persistent tokens/sec and TTFT degradation across Hosted, Dedicated and Private fleets during multi-region traffic shifts. Root cause traced to a recently deployed region-aware kernel scheduler + cold worker eviction policy that reduced effective prewarmed workers for larger-context models, causing coldstart thrash and queue head-of-line blocking. This ticket coordinates an emergency mitigation: staged rollback of scheduler routing changes for affected regions, immediate deployment of a hybrid queue coalescer to reduce microbatch churn, and a short-lived router warmup policy to pad capacity during regional failover windows.
comments: 2026-03-01: Pager alert from enterprise-customer 'NovaPay' about sustained TTFT regression (~2.5x) and tokens/sec drop after 09:40 UTC; increase in 5xxs and client retries observed. Ops annotated spike correlated with deployment rollout of scheduler v2.3.0.

2026-03-01 10:15 UTC: Triage call (on-call, infra, runtime, PM). Scoped impact: models with >8k context and quantized int8 paths hit worst. Affected environments: hosted-us-west, dedicated-eu-central, private-customer-42 (VPC). Decision: pause further v2.3 rollouts and start rollback in eu-central and us-west canaries.
2026-03-01 11:02 UTC: Rollback of scheduler change in eu-central completed; observed 40% TTFT improvement within 5 minutes for canary traffic. us-west rollback scheduled after safety checks.

2026-03-02: Engineering spike created to prototype hybrid queue coalescer (reduce tiny microbatches produced during cold worker spin-up). Prototype reduced average microbatch churn by ~60% in synthetic replay.

2026-03-03 08:40 UTC: Deployed router warmup policy (short-lived prewarm tokens with time-bound weight bump) to hosted-us-east and observed tokens/sec recover from 3k->8k for large-context tests in staging.

2026-03-04: Private customer patch: provided on-prem installable hotfix (kube init hook + prewarm image) for Customer-42; they reported 30% improvement and scheduled full update next maintenance window.

2026-03-06: Integration test uncovered regression where coalescer + kv-cache prefetch caused duplicate cache fills on corner path. Added idempotency guard in coalescer branch; unit tests updated (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127).

2026-03-08: Observability follow-up: added a Datadog composite dashboard (DD link: https://dd.example.com/dashboards/region-coldstart-275501) tracking per-region prewarm count, microbatch size distribution, TTFT p95 and tokens/sec. Alert thresholds tightened for p95 > 800ms for large-context models.

2026-03-10: Customer success: NovaPay follow-up call — they reported improved experience after rollbacks and staged hotfixes; still seeing intermittent spikes during cross-region failover (low frequency).

2026-03-12: Current status: hybrid queue coalescer in canary (hosted-eu); router warmup enabled for regions under failover windows; scheduler v2.3 pending code changes to respect large-context prewarm reservations. Next: land scheduler patch that integrates soft-reserve slots for large-context workers and hardens coalescer idempotency, then rollout with canary ramp and synthetic replay validation.
